subject: SIG follow-up: tenant-scoped SCIM mappings, RBAC playbook, and MFA enforcement
messages:
From: Alan Wu <alan.wu@broadleafhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@broadleafhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: SCIM mappings + MFA confirmation

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the initial SIG responses — Broadleaf's audit team reviewed your answers and flagged three items we'd like clarified before we close the access-controls section:

1) SCIM group mappings: we need an example mapping showing tenant-scoped groups -> Redwood roles (example: /tenants/acme/groups/engineering => role:engineer). Can you provide a small sample export or mapping table?

2) RBAC exceptions: describe your process for temporary elevated access (how are exceptions requested, approved, and timeboxed). Is there an automated attestation?

3) MFA enforcement: does MFA get enforced for service accounts used by CI/CD or just user accounts? If service accounts are exempted, what's the compensating control?

Can you send sample artifacts (mapping CSV, runbook snippet, or assertion example)? If it's easier we can hop on a 30m call.

Thanks,
Alan
Security Engineer
Broadleaf Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Wu <alan.wu@broadleafhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: SCIM mappings + MFA confirmation

Hi Alan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, details and artifacts attached:

1) SCIM group mappings: we attach a sample mapping export for a fictitious tenant (redwood-demo) that shows group -> role resolution and the SCIM path we populate. We support tenant-scoped group paths and map them to RBAC roles during provisioning. See redwood_scim_mapping.csv.

2) RBAC exceptions: temporary elevation uses our Authorization Exceptions flow: engineers request via the Console (request reason + duration), an approver (team owner or security) receives a notification, and the exception is granted with an automatic expiry (default 24 hours, configurable). All exceptions are logged and surfaced to periodic attestation. There's no fully automated attestation today; we run weekly exception reports and generate monthly attestation tasks for owners. Snippet attached: access-architecture-diagram.png shows flow.

3) MFA enforcement: MFA is enforced for all interactive user accounts. Service-to-service keys (used by CI/CD) do not have interactive MFA; instead we require short-lived tokens minted by our internal token service, scoped to a role, and issued after GitHub Actions OIDC or our internal Vault workflow. Compensating controls: short TTLs, strict IP whitelisting for deploy pipelines, and signature validation on tokens. See sso-assertion-sample.txt for an example assertion used in OIDC exchange.

I've CC'd Soojin and Neha in case you want doc-level references or policy text. If you'd like a short walkthrough I can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_scim_mapping.csv (CSV)
- access-architecture-diagram.png (PNG)
- sso-assertion-sample.txt (TXT)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: clarifications for Broadleaf — RBAC scope and attestation cadence

Marissa / Neha — looping in a couple quick clarifications before we send the final policy language to Broadleaf:

- The sample CSV I exported includes two special mapping rows for delegated admins (group path ends with /admins -> "role:tenant-admin"). We should call out that delegated admin grants are always limited to a tenant boundary and audited (no cross-tenant admin).
- For exceptions: remove the phrase "default 24 hours" and say "default 24 hours (configurable per org); security can extend with justification" — Broadleaf will likely want to know flexibility.
- For service accounts: can we add one line about our rotation window for OIDC-issued tokens (currently 15 minutes) and the CI/CD IP allowlist requirement? That helps with their compensating control question.

If you approve, I'll draft the final paragraph for the SIG "evidence" field and include the exact attestation cadence: weekly exception report, monthly owner attestations, quarterly audit review.

— Soojin
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: internal_rbac_notes.md referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Wu <alan.wu@broadleafhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: SCIM mappings + MFA confirmation

Hi Alan — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we expanded a couple points and attached the finalized text we use for SIG evidence. Highlights:

• SCIM & group mappings: attached CSV shows tenant-scoped paths and how they map to Redwood roles. Delegated admin groups are tenant-bound and logged; there is no cross-tenant elevation.
• RBAC exceptions: exceptions are requested in Console, require an approver, are timeboxed with an automatic expiry (default 24 hours, orgs may request longer with justification), are included in weekly exception reports, and are subject to monthly owner attestations and quarterly audit reviews.
• MFA & service accounts: MFA enforced for interactive users. Service accounts use OIDC/Vault short-lived tokens (15 minute TTL) and are subject to CI/CD IP allowlist and token signature verification.

I've attached the CSV, diagram, and assertion sample. If Broadleaf wants a quick 20–30m session to review the artifacts and walk through the attestation reports we can set that up next week.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference
